text:
support-lina: Heads-up — Acme (T-ACME-44) is hitting 429s on the reserved-west-2 dedicated pool since ~09:12. Customer says large nightly batch runs were cut off mid-job. Example error they sent: `error: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; code: 429; attempt_id: a1b2c3`

opsbot: Alert (reserved-west-2): 429 rate jumped 0.2% -> 34.8% in 7m (spike_id: spike-2026-03-17-0912). Autoscale did not add capacity; possible config-side rejection.

eng-matt: Can you paste tenant id + plan + any recent config/billing changes? Also looking for a trace_id from one of the 429s.

support-lina: Tenant: T-ACME-44, plan: dedicated-enterprise (reserved-west-2). They had a billing migration this morning (plan unify job at ~07:40). Customer trace sample: `trace=tr-9f8e7d`; they attached lines: 
```
2026-03-17T09:11:58Z request_id=rq-111 service=inference status=429 message="RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" tokens=234
2026-03-17T09:12:04Z request_id=rq-112 service=inference status=429 message="RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" tokens=145
```

sre-jen: Quick hypothesis: rate-profile mapping may have been created with an unexpected unit during the billing migration (minutes vs seconds). I'll query the quota-config. Command: 
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://config.internal/quotas/T-ACME-44 | jq .
```

eng-matt: I ran that query and snapshot below. Not pretty but illustrative: 
```
{
  "tenant_id": "T-ACME-44",
  "rate": 1000,
  "rate_unit": "per_second",
  "denom": 1
}
```
The rate looks like 1000/s. Billing migration was supposed to set 1000/min. So effective limit is 60x lower than intended. Looks like the migration omitted rate_unit metadata, and default fallback is `per_second`.

acct-ryan: Confirming — the migration script created a new profile without explicit `rate_unit`; older profiles used `per_minute`. New code path defaults to `per_second` when field missing (regression introduced in migration PR #4582).

support-lina: Oof. Need immediate mitigation for Acme. Customer is impacted on production batch window. What can we do right now?

eng-matt: Temporary fix: patch the quota entry to explicit `per_minute`. Patch command: 
```
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rate_unit":"per_minute"}' https://config.internal/quotas/T-ACME-44
```
Applied that at 09:15:22. API returned `200 OK` and new view: 
```
{"tenant_id":"T-ACME-44","rate":1000,"rate_unit":"per_minute","denom":60}
```

opsbot: Alert update: spike resolved. 429 rate dropped to 0.6% within 90s of patch. spike_id: spike-2026-03-17-0912 -> state: mitigated.

sre-jen: Root cause summary: billing migration created quota profiles without `rate_unit`; service defaulted to `per_second`. Impact = configured rates applied at wrong time unit (60x lower). Remediation: (1) backfill rate_unit during migration (hotfix PR), (2) add migration-time validation + unit tests, (3) add alert rule for sudden 429 % delta on reserved pools during migration windows. Filing postmortem and remediation ticket: PM-3127.

support-lina: Customer notified and confirmed batch resumed, they said jobs finished successfully after ~09:17. I'll close once they ack via support channel. :thumbsup: 

eng-matt: Follow-up — I pushed a hotfix to the migration job to include explicit `rate_unit` and added assert in CI. Will coordinate with acct to run backfill for other tenants touched by the migration.

acct-ryan: Running backfill now for the list provided by ops. ETA ~40m. I'll DM any problematic tenants.

support-lina: Thanks everyone. Logging this thread into PM-3127 and adding customer notes. Closing after final backfill confirmation.
